display.purpose: Landing H1, hero headlines, milestone heads. Always font-extrabold + tracking-tight.

headline.purpose: Section titles inside long pages and screens.

title.purpose: Card titles, modal heads, team names on TeamCard.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy, descriptions. Cap line length at 65–75ch on landing prose.

label.purpose: Eyebrow tags, MatchCard round headers, category labels. UPPERCASE + 0.1em letter-spacing.

mono.purpose: Chat-window chrome label ('Pick&Coach · copiloto IA'), debug strings only.

shadows.name: resting-card
shadows.purpose: Default MatchCard, secondary cards. Tailwind shadow-md.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Modal panels, dialog children. Tailwind shadow-xl.

shadows.name: team-card-heavy
shadows.purpose: Gradient TeamCard on HomeScreen. Tailwind shadow-2xl.

shadows.name: final-match-amber
shadows.purpose: The bracket's final match. Amber-tinted lift signals 'this is where it ends'.

shadows.name: pick-glow-rest
shadows.purpose: Pick chat box at rest. Animated; pulses to pick-glow-pulse.

shadows.name: pick-glow-pulse
shadows.purpose: Pick chat box at the peak of its 3s glow loop. Reserved for the landing demo.

motion.name: ease-out-snap
motion.purpose: Default exponential ease-out for state transitions and reveals. Snappy at the start, settles softly. No bounce, no elastic.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover state transitions on buttons, focus rings, color shifts.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Modal entrance (slide-up), card hover lifts, panel reveals.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Landing micro-scenes (fm-bubble-in, fm-fan-out, fm-tick-pop), step-in reveals.

motion.name: duration-loop-pick-thinking
motion.purpose: Pick 'thinking' typing-dots loop. Each dot offset 160ms from the previous.

motion.name: duration-loop-pick-glow
motion.purpose: Pick chat box heartbeat loop. Reserved for the landing hero.

motion.name: reduce-motion
motion.purpose: ALL decorative motion disables under this query (already enforced in src/index.css). Functional state transitions on focus/hover are still allowed; choreographed reveals must collapse to a no-op.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Phones in landscape, MatchCard switches to fixed 460px width.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Tablets. PublicNavbar shows full nav, mobile menu button hides. HomeScreen team carousel switches to grid.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Laptops. Landing hero switches from stacked to two-column, padding scales up.

narrative.overview: Pick&Coach is a basketball coaching workspace where Pick, an AI assistant, is already sat next to the coach on the bench. The interface enacts that relationship literally: orange CTAs that open like a teammate calling a play, electric-cyan controls that snap like a 24-second clock, amber that arrives when the trophy does, and motion that always narrates a basketball moment (the shot going up, the PDF resolving into a bracket, Pick thinking before responding). The atmosphere is court-side, alive, intentional. Sports-broadcast energy held together by craft. Every gradient, every shadow, every keyframe is doing a job. Decoration without narrative is the absolute failure mode. The system explicitly rejects generic SaaS templates, legacy coaching software, consumer fitness aesthetics, and plain AI chat shells.
keyCharacteristics: Two intentional accents: Court Orange for brand and Pick affordances, Score-Clock Cyan for in-app utility actions. Never collapsed into one.
Motion narrates. Every keyframe should be describable in a sentence.
Color does wayfinding: amber means trophy / your-team, purple means Pick, red means destructive.
Light by default in the private app; light-or-dark on public surfaces.
System fonts only. The voice carries the brand.

rules.name: The Two-Accent Rule
rules.body: Court Orange and Score-Clock Cyan are not interchangeable. Orange = brand and Pick. Cyan = in-app utility. Never use orange for an in-app save button. Never use cyan as the landing CTA. The day they collapse into one, the system loses its narrative.

rules.name: The Trophy-Amber Reservation
rules.body: Amber is for the trophy and what leads to it. If you are tempted to use amber as a generic warm accent, use Court Orange instead. Polluting amber kills its punch in brackets.

rules.name: The Pick-Purple Reservation
rules.body: Purple is Pick. Don't use it for users, calendars, scouting, or any non-AI surface. A future reader should be able to point at any purple in the product and say 'that is where Pick is talking.'

rules.name: The All-Caps-For-Eyebrows-Only Rule
rules.body: UPPERCASE plus tracking-widest is reserved for eyebrows and labels. Never set body, button, or heading text in caps. Caps stop being a signal if they are everywhere.

rules.name: The Heading-Pair Rule
rules.body: A pair of font-extrabold tracking-tight headings followed by a font-normal text-slate-600 body is the canonical block. If a screen has neither, it is drifting toward 'admin panel'.

rules.name: The Shadow-Means-State Rule
rules.body: Shadows are not decoration. A resting card uses shadow-md; on hover it goes shadow-lg. A modal is shadow-xl. If a shadow doesn't change between states or doesn't justify the lift, remove it.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Pick's-Heartbeat Rule
rules.body: The animated orange glow on the hero chat box is reserved for that specific surface. Don't replicate it on other cards or buttons. If everything glows, nothing does.

rules.name: The Two-Button Rule
rules.body: Inside /area-privada, never use the orange gradient as a primary action. On the landing or help, never use blue as a primary CTA. Cross the line and the narrative ('orange = Pick / brand, blue = utility') falls apart.

rules.name: The No-Nested-Cards Rule
rules.body: A MatchCard does not contain a sub-card. A TeamCard does not contain a sub-card. Nested cards are always wrong. If you need grouping inside a card, use spacing and dividers.

dos: Do keep Court Orange and Score-Clock Cyan in their lanes (orange for brand and Pick, cyan for in-app utility).
Do treat amber as a reservation. It appears with the trophy, the final, and 'your team's path', never as decoration.
Do make every animation describable as a sentence. If you cannot narrate it, delete it.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce from the first commit, the way src/index.css already does.
Do use system fonts. The voice carries the brand. Adding a custom typeface is a strategic decision, not a styling tweak.
Do keep Pick Purple as the AI-only color so future users can spot Pick by hue alone.
Do use Score-Clock Cyan focus rings (focus-visible:ring-blue-400) consistently. The blue focus ring is the system focus ring.
donts: Don't ship hero-metric templates (big number plus small label plus supporting stats plus gradient accent). That's the SaaS cliché PRODUCT.md explicitly rejects.
Don't make grids of identical icon-heading-text cards. Pick&Coach already has visually distinct card families (MatchCard, TeamCard, the playoff scrolltelling). Use them.
Don't use glassmorphism as a default surface treatment. The PublicNavbar uses one targeted backdrop-blur. That is the budget.
Don't rebuild Pick as a plain chat shell. The conversation is a layer over the workspace, not the workspace itself.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-l-4 colored stripes) as a decorative accent on cards or rows.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text over a gradient) as a headline treatment.
Don't mix the two oranges in the same screen. Pick one and stay consistent until the drift is resolved.
Don't add em dashes in copy. The system uses commas, colons, semicolons, periods, and parentheses.
Don't introduce a new accent color. Every additional color halves the meaning of the existing four.
Don't invent new shadow values. The vocabulary is shadow-md, shadow-lg, shadow-xl, shadow-2xl, plus the amber-tinted final-match shadow and the Pick glow.
Don't use the orange CTA gradient on a private-app surface. If a private screen 'needs' it for emphasis, the screen has a layout problem, not a color problem.
